title: Late harvest
subtitle: Sweet Gewürztraminer
objectives: Explain why Gewürztraminer suits sweet styles

steps.title: Vendanges Tardives
steps.body: Alsace's Vendanges Tardives, VT, means late harvest. Grapes stay on the vine into late autumn, concentrating sugar. Gewürztraminer VT needs a minimum potential alcohol of about 15.3%, around 257 g/l of sugar at harvest. The wines can be dry, off-dry or sweet, rich and intensely perfumed.

steps.title: Sélection de Grains Nobles
steps.body: Sélection de Grains Nobles, SGN, is made from berries affected by noble rot, picked one by one. Minimum sugar is higher, about 18.2% potential alcohol for Gewürztraminer. SGN wines are lusciously sweet, with honey, candied fruit and spice, and can age for decades.

steps.prompt: Order these Alsace Gewürztraminer styles from least to most concentrated.
steps.explanation: Later picking and noble rot concentrate sugar further.

steps.title: Why it suits sweetness
steps.body: Gewürztraminer's high natural sugar and intense aroma suit late harvest styles. Its weakness, low acidity, is a challenge: the best VT and SGN come from top sites and vintages where acidity is preserved. Without it, the wines can feel heavy.
steps.highlight: High sugar, but acidity is key

steps.prompt: What is Sélection de Grains Nobles made from?
steps.explanation: SGN uses botrytised berries, selected one by one.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Vendanges Tardives is late harvest, dry to sweet
SGN uses noble rot berries and is lusciously sweet
Acidity decides the best sweet Gewürztraminer
